subject: Onboarding: Uptime/Latency Measurement & Dashboard Access
messages:
From: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@exemplarhealth.com>
To: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, procurement@exemplarhealth.com
Date: 2027-03-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Vendor questionnaire: how you measure uptime/latency (Exemplar onboarding)

Hi Grace,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at Exemplar is comfortable with Redwood's performance profile but procurement needs a bit more detail for our SRE and security review. Attached is a short spreadsheet showing what we need: exact SLO definitions, measurement windows, alert thresholds, and the way we'll get access to dashboards and raw telemetry.

Can you confirm:
- How is 'availability' defined at the API layer (what HTTP codes / error classes are excluded)?
- What window do you use to calculate uptime (e.g., 30d rolling, calendar month)?
- Where will we be able to see latency p95/p99 and per-route error rates?
- If we request an exception (e.g., allowed maintenance window), how is that documented and what is the approval flow?

We need the answers by EOD Wednesday to keep the procurement timeline. I've attached the spreadsheet for your procurement/legal team to fill out.

Best,
Sasha
Director of IT Operations
Exemplar Health

[Attachment: uptime_dashboard_access_request.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

From: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
To: Sasha Patel <sasha.patel@exemplarhealth.com>
Cc: jordan.blake@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-01T13:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire: how you measure uptime/latency (Exemplar onboarding)

Sasha — thanks for the clear list and the spreadsheet. I've filled the first pass and added comments where we usually need a quick sync with SRE for specifics. High-level answers below; the filled workbook is attached.

Key points:
- Availability definition: Redwood counts requests as successful when they return 2xx with a valid model response payload. Client-visible errors (4xx) are considered failures for availability if they stem from our runtime (rate-limit responses attributable to customer rate limits are flagged separately). 5xx and transport errors contribute to availability failures.
- Measurement window: default is a 30-day rolling window for SLA reporting; for contractual SLOs we can also report calendar-month aggregates.
- Latency metrics: p50/p95/p99 are recorded at the per-route and per-model level. Dashboards expose per-route percentiles and sampled histograms. We publish 1m and 5m rolling summaries and store 60 days of high-fidelity metrics; 13 months available as aggregated rollups.
- Access: customers are invited to a read-only project dashboard in Redwood Console. For procurement, we provide a time-limited Grafana invite or a PDF export; for Dedicated/Private customers we support direct Grafana read-only integration via SAML.
- Exception flow: maintenance windows and temporary SLA exceptions are requested via the Console's 'Service Requests' flow. The request is routed to Account Engineering and Product Ops; written approvals are recorded in the customer's audit trail (Doc ID stored).

I've added two items where Jordan can add technical details about alerting and instrumentation. If you want a live run-through of the dashboard, I'm available tomorrow at 10:00 PT.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
grace.oconnor@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Vendor questionnaire: how you measure uptime/latency (Exemplar onboarding)

Hi Sasha — adding the instrumentation/alerting detail Grace mentioned. A few concrete bullets to paste into your procurement workbook: 

- Sampling & aggregation: per-request traces are sampled (default 1%) for full latency histograms; we compute percentile estimates from the high-fidelity stream and correct bias via reservoir techniques. Aggregates at 1m granularity feed dashboards; raw traces retained for 30 days.
- Error classification: automatic classifiers tag errors (runtime OOM, model tokenizer errors, infra connectivity). We map those to procurement-friendly buckets: AvailabilityFailure, DegradedPerformance, ConfigError.
- Alerting thresholds (recommended starter set):
  * SLO burn rate alert: 5-minute burn > 4x for a sustained 15 minutes
  * Latency p95 increase: >40% over baseline for 5m
  * Availability drop: >0.5% absolute drop in 30-day rolling window
- On-call and escalation: Account Engineering triages first 30 minutes; operations engineers engage within 2 hours for incidents affecting >1% of traffic. We provide incident postmortems and uptime corrections if the root cause is within Redwood's control.

If procurement wants the precise metric IDs and the Grafana panel json, we can export those as a zipped artifacts bundle. I can prepare the bundle after we confirm the scope (hosted vs Dedicated).

—Jordan
Senior Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
